decisions.reason: Substantive coverage of the NoisyTCP advisory: Hyunwoo Kim's CVE-2026-99288, oss-security disclosure after embargo, unauthenticated remote kernel crash. Same story as the existing masto items, so it attaches rather than minting a new one. No in-the-wild exploitation claimed, only a reliable DoS primitive, so no exploitation field.

Link-hijacking campaign against short links used by Burger King, McDonald's and the FBI is a real brand-abuse and redirect-malware story, not an explainer. Thin reddit link submission, so it stays attached to the existing story rather than growing it.

AWS's own confirmation of the Nov 15 US-EAST-1 incident: 11 services degraded, authentication and sign-up failures, final resolution at 6:53 AM PST. Availability incident with broad customer impact and no attribution to an attacker, so it stays in its existing single-event story.

Amazon threat intelligence ran decoy servers and captured attacker AI agents scanning exposed LiteLLM, One API and Dify instances for provider API keys, then reusing stolen keys to fuel further searching. Named targets and a named research team, worth a story.

Thailand-targeted LOTUSLITE V2 campaign using an Indo-Pacific security assessment lure and legitimate PDFgear as the delivery vehicle; technical analysis with high confidence on the .NET implant and an assessed Mustang Panda link. Real intrusion activity.

Retadup USB worm revived as a CoffeeLoader delivery chain: NSIS installer drops a patched 7z.dll loaded via rundll32.exe, carrying self-decrypting shellcode from a new Armoury packer variant that swapped OpenCL for OpenGL GPU decryption. First-party technical research with concrete implementation detail.

Kaspersky ICS CERT investigation, triggered by the victim developer in June 2025, of a months-long compromise of a Russian software developer's build infrastructure and code-signing server by BO Team (Black Owl, Hoody Hyena). Exploitation of Log4Shell in VMware vCenter is the entry vector the reporting names.

CVE-2021-44228.evidence: Kaspersky ICS CERT attributes the compromise to BO Team, who exploited Log4Shell in VMware vCenter to reach the code-signing server; the actor maintained access for months before discovery.
